extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. The dataset consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish).
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consists of 8 languages. Audio files downloaded from LibriVox were downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss. The segmentation process involved running inference on audio to generate viterbi token sequences with timestamps, then selecting the longest silence duration within 10-20 sec range to split audio at the mid point of the silence chunk.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobook data, most of which being based on the Project Gutenberg text data. For English, 60K hours of audiobooks were read from four major website domains - gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org and hathitrust.org. For other languages, text sources were extracted from various domains using parsers, manual copying from browsers, or extraction from .pdf/.epub books using pdftotext tool.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Numbers in the text were handled by aligning the matched text from the book with the pseudo label and replacing the numbers in the matched text with the corresponding aligned words from the pseudo label. Heuristics were used to deal with hyphens and apostrophes, including removing end-of-line hyphenation and joining word parts, and replacing rare words with hyphens or apostrophes based on alignment with pseudo labels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text normalization was performed including NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters like punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols. Hyphens used for end-of-line hyphenation were removed and word parts joined into single words. Valid unicode characters were filtered based on language orthography. Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments. Candidate transcripts were filtered if WER between candidate transcript and pseudo label was >40%.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo labels were generated for segmented audio samples by performing beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model on acoustic models. Transcript retrieval involved finding true target labels from source text using TF-IDF similarity score on bigrams and Smith-Waterman alignment with matching score of 2 and substitution, insertion, deletion score of -1. Human evaluation was performed on development and test sets where transcribers listened to audio while looking at transcripts and corrected clear and obvious errors.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Acoustic models trained using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss for segmentation. wav2letter@anywhere framework for streaming inference. 4-gram language models for beam-search decoding to generate pseudo labels. Gender classifier using SVM with RBF kernel trained on LibriSpeech data (1172 speakers) consuming 40-dimensional log-filterbank features.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender information was collected for speakers using a gender classifier (SVM with RBF kernel). Speakers were labeled and balanced by gender in development and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors believe such a large transcribed dataset will open new avenues in ASR and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. The dataset promotes open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and in multilingual ASR.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is read-speech only, derived from audiobooks. For English, the MLS development and test sets are chosen to be harder than LibriSpeech dev-/test-other partitions, with speakers having WER higher than 80% of the ones in dev-other sets. For Polish, the OOV rate is 13% which negatively impacts WER when performing LM decoding with constrained lexicon. The pseudo label generation may not always have correct transcription of the audio.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. It includes train, development and test splits. Limited supervision datasets are provided (10 hour set, 1 hour set, and six 10-minute sets) to create standard benchmarks for low resource training. The dataset can be used for training, testing, and validation of ASR models. Language models and baseline ASR models are provided for all languages.
